notes: Migrated on 2026-11-11 to the current layout: the indeterminate queries and worlds were removed (TBox records have determinate derived queries only), a third propositional query was added (negation, conjunction with a true side fact, disjunction with a false one) and each derived query now names its task, fact and derivability with evidence. TBox rule edit. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is the definition of a first-class lever, stated in general form in textbooks and Wikipedia ("first class lever" 1,681 in Dolma, "fulcrum in the middle" 897). Counterfactual: the load in the middle is the second-class layout, a plausible confusion, clearly false here. The derived queries name made-up tools (Brannick grip, Tollan arm, Corvin lifter) that the model knows only by their class (inheritance, 2 hops); the third is an application, a design choice that names the elements in plain words (pivot, where she pushes, the object lifted) so it does not repeat the edit's wording. Cross-lingual questions rephrased after two models missed each: the Chinese one asks which of the three elements lies between the other two, without listing them (a listed choice would contain its own answer), the Spanish one uses the standard textbook terms punto de apoyo, potencia and resistencia (the earlier "carga" and "fuerza" drew wrong answers). The seesaw and scissors checks went with the indeterminate queries (all four models had also called scissors a second- or third-class lever). Near query changed: three models answered the third-class lever question wrongly, so it now asks the name of the lever's pivot, the fulcrum, which an edit that leaks would not change and which differs from the new answer. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the side facts need checks.
